A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GNNXEMPLAR research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A and B are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, parameter and architecture studies, and a 60-participant survey comparing explanation modalities.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and human-study results, including benchmark Tables 2 and 4–8 and survey Table 3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 3 retain the same reverse-k-NN coverage selection, sampling approximation, LLM rule generation, self-refinement, and Boolean aggregation. The expanded definitions do not document a changed computational procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate TAGCora, Citeseer, WikiCS, ogbn-arxiv, Amazon-ratings, Questions, Minesweeper, and BA-Shapes. The appendix studies and 60-participant explanation-modality survey also retain the same task and population coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 6–8 retain GNNInterpreter, GCNeuron, and GLGExplainer in the same comparisons. Figure 3 retains random exemplar selection and zero-shot rule generation. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The stated data splits, GNN architectures, 250-epoch training, explanation hyperparameters, evaluation metrics, and five-question survey protocol remain unchanged in Section 4.1 and Appendices A.1–A.2 and B.

E4.justification: Both retain the two Figure 3 ablations, parameter sweeps in Figures 17–19, architecture comparison in Table 5, and rule and failure-case analyses. The parameter and architecture appendix sections are renumbered without new analyses.

E5.justification: The uncertainty displays, Figure 17's five-run statement, and binomial and McNemar analyses are unchanged. The new checklist points to existing statistical reporting without disclosing additional runs, seeds, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 2–8 and the ablation and sensitivity plots retain their values and result entries. For example, TAGCora fidelity remains 0.83 ± 0.01, and survey preferences remain 200 text versus 100 subgraph choices. Qualitative rule and diagnostic findings also match.

T1.justification: Definitions 3–4 add explicit distance/population thresholds for exemplars and Boolean-predicate formalization of signatures. New Appendix A.6 extends the coverage argument to approximate reverse-k-NN sets and claims an additive-error bound for estimated coverage. The original sampling lemma, NP-hardness proof, and exact-coverage proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about exemplar-based global explanation, greedy coverage selection, LLM-derived rules, fidelity, scalability, and preference for textual explanations.

C2.justification: Interpretations of baseline failures, ablation outcomes, parameter sensitivity, and the Questions homophily shortcut are retained. Section 5 preserves the same limitation concerning access to fine-grained internal mechanisms and the same proposed future direction.

D1.justification: The new checklist discloses that survey participation was voluntary and anonymous, sensitive information was not requested, and institutional policy did not require IRB approval. These document the existing study; hardware, hyperparameters, training details, prompt content, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds introductory citations to GraphReach and the global counterfactual explainer/GCFExplainer publications. This modestly expands acknowledgment of prior work without substantively changing the research positioning or baseline rationale.

P1.justification: v2 adds a NeurIPS checklist, expands local explanations around the definitions and approximation argument, and updates affiliations, acknowledgments, notation, and minor wording. The main research narrative and experimental organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: Tables 6–8 are grouped together instead of interspersed with survey screenshots. Representative-power formulas receive clearer display formatting, prompt/code panels are reformatted, and several floats move. The existing figures and tables retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves exposition and documentation through more explicit definitions, discussion of sampled coverage, survey disclosures, and better grouping of appendix results. The theoretical benefit is limited: Appendix A.6 invokes a set-level error bound that the cited node-level Lemma 1 does not explicitly establish. The unchanged empirical evidence and this remaining gap limit the overall gain.
